chunks: And Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from al-Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Abu Dawood al-Mustarriq, from Ali ibn Maymoon as-Sa'igh, from Ibn Abi Ya'foor who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Three people, whom Allah will not speak to on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He purify, and for them is a painful chastisement: One who claims for himself an imamate from Allah that is not his, one who denies an imam appointed by Allah, and one who claims that these two have a share in Islam.'
ai.seo_question: Who are the three people Allah will not speak to on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: Compiled by al-Nu'mani in *Kitab al-Ghayba*, this hadith highlights the critical Shia doctrine of *Imamah* by identifying three groups doomed to divine neglect: false claimants, deniers, and those who conflate the two. It underscores the theological necessity of distinguishing between the divinely appointed Imam and mere political pretenders, a key concern during the Minor and Major Gheebah periods. The inclusion of 'deniers' alongside 'false claimants' emphasizes that both error and denial of the rightful Imam constitute a loss of Islamic identity.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (3) Muhammad bin Ya’qoob narrated from al-Husayn bin Muhammad from Mu’alla bin Muhammad from Abu Dawood al-Mustaraqq from Ali bin Maymoon as-Sa’igh from Abu Ya’foor

that Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as) had said: “There are three persons, whom Allah will not speak to on the Day of Resurrection nor will He purify and shall have a painful chastisement; one, who pretends the divine imamate while he is not an imam, one, who denies an imam appointed by Allah and the third one is he, who claims that these two ones are faithful Muslims.”
